definition: A variant of gradient descent that updates parameters using a randomly sampled subset (mini-batch) of the training data instead of the full dataset.
details: SGD trades off exact gradient computation for speed and the ability to train on datasets too large to fit in memory at once, at the cost of noisier updates.

explainer.lead: Stochastic gradient descent is a variant of gradient descent that updates parameters using a randomly sampled subset (mini-batch) of the training data instead of the full dataset. It matters because it is fast and can train on datasets too large to fit in memory at once.

tiers.eli5: Instead of reading the whole book before taking a step, you glance at a few pages, adjust, and keep going.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use mini-batch updates to train models quickly on large datasets. A pitfall is that the updates are noisier than exact gradient computation, so the sampling trades exactness for speed.
tiers.paperLevel: Parameters are updated from a randomly sampled mini-batch rather than the full dataset; the known limit is noisier updates in exchange for speed and feasibility on datasets too large to hold in memory.

explainer.example: A model with a training set too large for memory takes each update from a small random mini-batch rather than the full set.
